Our team is expanding and we are looking for a dynamic and driven Quality Manager to join a fast-growing global company in the automotive sector. The Quality Manager oversees all aspects of quality assurance and quality control, ensuring that products and services meet customer expectations and comply with regulatory requirements.
Key Responsibilities
Quality Management System (QMS) – Maintain and continuously optimize the IATF 16949 and VDA 6.3 quality system across the Lewisburg plant.
Customer Audits and PPAP – Lead customer audits, including PPAP and MMOG/LE processes for original equipment manufacturers.
Quality Planning – Develop specialized Control Plans, Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and inspection standards (SIP) for aluminum components.
Process Quality Control – Monitor critical parameters of aluminum die-casting, extrusion and welding processes; implement Statistical Process Control (SPC) and anomaly analysis, such as porosity and dimensional deviations.
Problem Solving – Promote 8D and 5 Whys methodologies to address recurring quality issues and reduce Parts Per Million (PPM) defects.
Supplier Quality – Evaluate the quality capabilities of aluminum material and mold suppliers through Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE) audits; manage supplier corrective action requests (SCARs) in a closed-loop system.
Customer Quality – Handle customer quality complaints, including claims processing, and provide regular monthly quality reports (QBR).
Team Leadership – Lead quality engineers and Quality Control (QC) teams; enhance inspection efficiency by introducing automated inspection technologies.
Cost of Quality – Manage Cost of Quality (COQ) and minimize scrap rates.
Requirements
Minimum of eight years of quality management experience for automotive aluminum components, with familiarity with the defect patterns associated with die-casting and extrusion processes.
Proficiency in the APQP/PPAP process and aluminum part inspection techniques, such as X-ray and spectral analysis.
Expertise in Minitab and the seven major QC tools, with the ability to make data-driven decisions.
Fluency in English, as the role requires interaction with global clients.
Must be at least 18 years of age and legally authorized to work in the United States.
Preferred Qualifications (a Plus)
Experience in OEM or Tier 1 aluminum parts projects.
Proficiency in Chinese, an advantage for collaboration with group and China-based teams.
MINIMUM EDUCATION / FIELD OF STUDY
Bachelor’s degree or higher in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Quality Management or a related field.
KEY TO BEING SUCCESSFUL IN THIS ROLE
A data-driven approach to quality, using SPC, PPM and Cost of Quality to prioritize improvements.
Disciplined problem solving, applying 8D and 5 Whys to eliminate root causes of recurring issues.
Strong customer focus and the ability to lead audits and manage complaints with global OEM clients.
Leadership of quality engineers and QC teams, with a drive to introduce automated inspection.
Good teamwork and communication skills in a multicultural team.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING ENVIRONMENT
Work performed in both the office and on the manufacturing floor, including standing and walking; hearing protection, safety glasses, safety footwear and other required PPE are worn on the floor.
Exposure to noise and moving equipment in die-casting, extrusion and welding areas.
Occasionally lift up to 25 lbs.
Regular computer use for quality data analysis, reporting and documentation.
Ability to perform the essential functions of this position, with or without reasonable accommodation.
WHY WORK FOR MINTH?
Minth Group is a global leader in automotive trim and structural components, and you can build your career in quality management with a growing North American team.
International development platform – Be part of a global automotive supplier with 78 plants worldwide and a regional North American headquarters in Wixom, Michigan.
Dynamic and efficient team – Work with production, engineering and supply chain colleagues in a fast-growing organization.
All-round personal improvement – Grow your skills in quality systems, audits and continuous improvement.
Personalized humanistic care – A workplace that values and supports its people.
Diversified working atmosphere – A multicultural, multinational workplace where different backgrounds and perspectives are valued.
Modern office setting – A modern, well-equipped working environment.
Competitive compensation package – Competitive pay and benefits for a full-time, stable career.

About Rivian
Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.
As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.
Role Summary
The Sr. Manager, Planning & Scheduling, Production Facilities is the technical and people leader accountable for integrated master scheduling, schedule analytics, EVMS, and schedule aspects of procurement for Rivian’s Production Facilities current mega‑projects and future factory campuses.
They own the P6 schedule architecture, critical‑path and float analysis, cross‑functional interfaces and schedule‑risk integration that underpins commissioning milestones and production ramp readiness. This role requires portfolio‑level integration across manufacturing, OEM integrators, shutdowns, commissioning, long‑lead procurement, and lender‑visible milestones on $2B+ programs.
Because schedule is the single integrated view of factory readiness, this role is mission‑critical to Rivian’s ability to launch vehicles on time, protect revenue, and meet DOE and lender expectations.
Responsibilities
Expected scope
Direct responsibility for integrated master schedules covering >$1B in annual CAPEX across one or more mega‑programs.
Ownership of logic‑linked schedules across design, permitting, procurement, construction, OEM installation, commissioning, and handover, including multi‑campus dependencies and long‑lead procurement chains.
EVMS Implementation: Architect and deploy comprehensive Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS) tailored to specific project lifecycles, including short-term rolling scopes and long-term EPC phases
Leadership of a team of schedulers and planning analysts; close integration with cost, procurement, VDC, risk, and PM organizations.
Integrated master scheduling, procurement scheduling & architecture
Own the P6 schedule architecture for assigned programs, including logic linking of facilities work, OEM integrators, commissioning, manufacturing ramp, and all critical procurement activities (RFPs, evaluations, awards, fabrication, delivery, installation windows).
Develop and maintain Level 1–4 schedules that connect enterprise milestones (funding releases, DOE gates, SOP) to detailed construction, commissioning, and procurement tasks, ensuring full technical traceability from field work and vendor actions to portfolio commitments.
Software Proficiency: Advanced knowledge of EVMS-enabling tools such as Cobra, Unifier, or Ecosys
Ensure consistent schedule coding standards, calendars, and WBS structures across campuses and programs to enable portfolio roll‑ups and benchmarking.
Schedule analytics, EVMS & performance management
Run critical path, near‑critical path, float‑erosion, and what‑if simulations to support capital sequencing, risk mitigation, acceleration, and recovery planning, including procurement‑driven paths (long‑lead equipment, fabrication, logistics, customs, site readiness).
Implement and maintain Earned Value Management at program scale, integrating schedule and cost data to provide objective insights on progress, productivity, and forecasted outcomes.
Define and manage schedule KPIs (SPI, forecasted completion, constraint burn‑down, procurement lead‑time adherence, variance‑to‑plan) and drive corrective actions with PMs, Procurement, and functional leaders.
Interface, shutdown, commissioning & procurement integration
Coordinate complex interfaces between facilities construction, tool installation, OEM integrators, production trials, phased handovers, and procurement deliverables, ensuring schedule logic reflects operational realities and risk mitigations.
Own schedule strategies for shutdowns, cutovers, and brownfield interventions, including contingency plans and alternative work sequences to protect production while executing upgrades.
Partner with Quality, Commissioning, Manufacturing Engineering, and Procurement to align schedule milestones with readiness criteria, vendor commitments, and risk mitigations, so factories transition smoothly from construction to sustained operations.
Schedule‑risk & quantitative analysis
Lead or co‑lead QSRA (Quantitative Schedule Risk Analysis) at major design, procurement, and construction inflection points; integrate outputs into float strategies, contingency, management reserve, and procurement strategies.
Maintain a live risk register for schedule and procurement threats and opportunities; quantify impacts and mitigation benefits, and ensure alignment with cost, scope, and contracting decisions.
Technology, VDC & visualization
Integrate schedules with VDC and 4D/5D/6D models (ACC, Bexel, Navisworks, point cloud models) to simulate construction, commissioning, and procurement‑driven sequences for mega‑projects.
Partner with Facilities Technology and VDC to ensure data flows cleanly between P6, VDC, PMIS, and reporting systems, enabling visual, data‑driven decision‑making for leadership on critical path, procurement bottlenecks, and risk.
Reporting, governance & communication
Develop and maintain standard schedule and procurement‑schedule reporting packs (dashboards, look‑ahead reports, variance narratives) for PMs, Directors, Executives, and lenders. Provide clear early‑warning signals on emerging schedule and procurement risks, recovery opportunities, and cross‑program impacts, especially for critical launches such as our current Stanton Springs North project outside Atlanta.
Mentor schedulers, planners, and project teams on mega‑project scheduling and procurement‑integration best practices, elevating schedule literacy across Production Facilities and partner organizations so schedule becomes a trusted technical instrument, not just a reporting artifact.
Qualifications
10–15+ years in project controls with a primary focus on planning & scheduling for complex industrial or mega‑projects; at least one full lifecycle from FEL through commissioning in a lead role.
Deep, hands‑on expertise in Primavera P6 and related scheduling tools.
Experience implementing comprehensive EVMS, 4D/5D/6D scheduling, and portfolio‑level reporting for owner‑operators or EPCs.
Architected and drove strategic implementation of an Earned Value Management System (EVMS) for multi-billion dollar mega-programs, including defining scope, reviewing proposals, and securing executive alignment on the final implementation path.
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, project management, or related technical discipline; advanced degrees and certifications (e.g., PSP, PMI‑SP) preferred.
Pay Disclosure
The salary range for this role is USD $161,000-$213,260 for Georgia based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.
The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.

Join Axon and be a Force for Good.
At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.
Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.
Your Impact
You will lead a team of Mission Engineers who serve as Axon’s embedded builders and operational partners inside strategic public safety agencies. Mission Engineers work face-to-face with the people doing the work, diagnose how the agency operates, and build the workflows, automations, integrations, and AI-enabled solutions that measurably improve it.
As Senior Manager, you will create the environment in which that work succeeds. You will coach experienced individual contributors, set a clear bar for technical delivery and agency partnership, and help the team turn ambiguous field problems into secure, maintainable solutions that reach production and earn sustained adoption. You will stay close enough to the portfolio to recognize patterns, anticipate risk, and connect what the team learns in the field back to Product, Engineering, and the broader organization.
Success is reflected in agencies becoming more capable, Mission Engineers growing into trusted transformation leaders, and strong field solutions becoming reusable patterns that benefit customers beyond a single engagement. Axon’s mission is to Protect Life, and this team is one of the most direct ways we advance that mission alongside the agencies we serve.
What You’ll Do
Location: Southeast US Regionally based with Travel up to 40%
Reports to: Senior Director, Customer Deployment & Mission Engineering
Direct Reports: Individual Contributors
Lead, Coach, and Develop Mission Engineers
Lead and develop a distributed team of embedded Mission Engineers working across strategic agency environments
Coach individual contributors through complex technical decisions, ambiguous customer problems, executive conversations, and high-stakes delivery moments
Establish clear expectations for ownership, technical quality, onsite partnership, production delivery, adoption, documentation, and measurable agency impact
Build individualized development plans and create opportunities for Mission Engineers to expand their technical range, executive presence, and transformation leadership
Foster a culture of curiosity, candor, responsible experimentation, continuous learning, and shared accountability
Support thoughtful team growth by selecting and onboarding people who can both build practical solutions and earn credibility with agency stakeholders
Set the Bar for Agency Outcomes
Ensure Mission Engineers begin with the agency’s mission, operational workflow, and desired outcome before selecting or building a solution
Require clear baselines, success criteria, and adoption measures so impact is demonstrated rather than assumed
Guide the team from discovery through production use, iteration, handoff, and sustained adoption
Help Mission Engineers balance immediate agency needs with secure, maintainable, and scalable solution design
Reinforce that success means the agency is more capable—not that one individual has become indispensable
Own a Strategic Mission Engineering Portfolio
Maintain visibility across strategic agencies, active builds, adoption progress, technical risk, and emerging operational needs
Match Mission Engineer capability and level to agency complexity, transformation opportunity, and stakeholder environment
Use operating reviews and portfolio data to identify delivery risks, recurring friction, adoption barriers, and opportunities for reuse
Step into critical situations with structure and calm while coaching the accountable Mission Engineer to remain in ownership
Drive consistent execution across embedded engagements without forcing every agency problem into the same playbook
Advance Technical and AI-Enabled Delivery
Maintain sufficient fluency across SaaS, cloud services, APIs, enterprise integrations, hardware, data, and modern AI tooling to coach technical decisions and challenge weak reasoning
Help the team decide when to configure the platform, when to extend it, and when a net-new build is justified
